html:
The year 69 CE, when four men ruled Rome one after another: Galba, Otho, Vitellius and Vespasian. It was the first civil war of the Roman Empire.

Nero killed himself in June 68 CE, and the Julio-Claudian line ended. Then:

  • Galba, governor of Spain, became emperor but was stingy and harsh, and in January 69 CE the Praetorian Guard killed him;
  • Otho, who had paid them, took his place, but the Rhine legions had already proclaimed their own general;
  • Vitellius beat Otho at the first battle of Bedriacum in April, and Otho killed himself;
  • in July the eastern armies proclaimed Vespasian; troops from the Danube invaded Italy, won the second battle of Bedriacum in October and stormed Rome in December, and Vitellius was killed.

The temple of Jupiter on the Capitol burned in the fighting. Tacitus wrote that the "secret of empire" was out: an emperor could be made somewhere other than Rome, by the armies. Vespasian founded the Flavian dynasty and restored order.
